# Kill9 by Aditya Mali

Official product page: https://www.adityamali.com/cafe/kill9
Developer: Aditya Mali — https://www.adityamali.com/about
Source code: https://github.com/adityamali/kill9
Category: macOS developer utility
Platform: macOS 13.0 or later, Apple silicon and Intel
Technologies: SwiftUI and AppKit

Kill9 is a native macOS menu bar utility that finds processes listening on local TCP ports, identifies associated development projects when metadata is available, and lets users stop those processes through a graphical interface. It helps developers free occupied localhost ports and investigate EADDRINUSE errors without typing Terminal commands.

## How it works

Open the KILL9 menu bar panel to inspect detected development listeners. Check the port, runtime, PID, and project information before stopping a process. Kill9 uses lsof to inspect TCP listeners. Automatic discovery focuses on development servers owned by the current user. UDP and non-listening TCP connections are outside this workflow. Port inclusion and exclusion filters customize discovery.

Project identification uses working-directory and project metadata. A package.json name is used when available, with project-folder inference as a fallback. Not every process can be associated with a project.

Stop sends SIGTERM, allowing an opportunity for graceful shutdown. If the same process remains after refresh, Force becomes available. It sends SIGKILL only when explicitly clicked. Escalation is not automatic. Kill9 checks ownership and process start time before signaling. It does not stop processes owned by other users. Stopping a process affects every port it owns, and a supervisor may restart it.

## Installation

Use the download link on the official product page. Extract the ZIP, move Kill9.app to Applications, and open it. Kill9 appears in the menu bar rather than a conventional app window or Dock icon. The current app requires macOS 13.0 or later and supports Apple silicon and Intel Macs. There is no Windows or Linux version.

## macOS Terminal alternative

Inspect port 3000:
    lsof -nP -iTCP:3000 -sTCP:LISTEN

Check the command and PID, then request shutdown of the verified process:
    kill -TERM <PID>

Replace <PID> with the numeric process ID. Inspect the port again. Use kill -KILL <PID> (kill -9) only for an unresponsive, verified process when forced termination is appropriate. Forced termination does not allow cleanup. Substitute 8080, 5173, or another TCP port number as needed.

EADDRINUSE means the requested address and port are already in use. The existing service may be functioning normally. Stop it only if appropriate, or configure the new server to use another port.

For installation links, FAQs, and current product information, use the official product page.
